sample_unit: patient questions (each submitted to four chatbots)

links.outcome: Readability of chatbot CBCT patient information versus recommended health literacy thresholds
links.effect: Responses from advanced models frequently exceeded recommended health literacy thresholds; readability varied substantially between platforms; no chatbot met all criteria for optimal patient-directed communication.
links.quote: While advanced models demonstrated higher informational quality and reliability, their responses frequently exceeded recommended health literacy thresholds.

links.outcome: Reading grade level of chatbot-generated patient materials relative to user reading level
links.effect: Responses frequently exceeded recommended health literacy thresholds on Flesch-Kincaid, Flesch Reading Ease and Gunning Fog measures; significant differences among chatbots (p < 0.05).
links.quote: While advanced models demonstrated higher informational quality and reliability, their responses frequently exceeded recommended health literacy thresholds.

screen.reason: Evaluates commercial LLM chatbots on their readability and quality for patient education regarding dental CBCT queries, but does not test a specific guardrail or deployment practice.
